classification.spec_type_rationale: existing Tabs.css renders accent-as-text (real) plus stale design tokens; fix = token sync + 2 accent swaps

spec_seeds.overview: The working-tabs strip renders two accent-colored roles below WCAG 2.1 AA, and separately the app's design tokens are STALE relative to design/styles.css (their declared source of truth): the muted and faint text tokens were already darkened for AA at the source but never synced into src/renderer/styles/tokens.css. This spec (1) syncs the three drifted token values to design/styles.css — which brings every --text-muted / --text-faint text consumer app-wide to AA in one edit — and (2) swaps the two genuine accent-on-light sites in Tabs.css to var(--text). No new token and no contract amendment are needed.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The design-token stylesheet shall define the muted and faint text tokens at the darkened values from the design source.
acceptance_criteria.verification_command: grep -q -- '--text-muted: #6c6c75' src/renderer/styles/tokens.css && grep -q -- '--text-faint: #6e6e77' src/renderer/styles/tokens.css && grep -q -- '--text-faint: #787881' src/renderer/styles/tokens.css

acceptance_criteria.statement: The system shall preserve the existing token names and semantics, introducing no new color token.
WHILE either theme is active, the Tabs strip shall keep the active-tab and inactive-tab labels visually distinct.
The system shall bring every muted and faint text role to the WCAG AA contrast minimum by syncing the token values to the design source.
WHILE either theme is active, the active-tab label shall meet the WCAG AA contrast minimum for normal text by using var(--text), which the tabbar variant inherits.
WHILE a tab is active, the active-tab badge text shall meet the WCAG AA contrast minimum for normal text on the accent-soft background by using var(--text).
WHILE either theme is active, the inactive-tab label shall meet the WCAG AA contrast minimum for normal text via the synced var(--text-muted).
WHILE either theme is active, the close-button icon shall meet the WCAG AA non-text contrast minimum via the synced var(--text-faint).
WHILE a tab is marked dirty, the dirty-state indicator shall meet the WCAG AA non-text contrast minimum via the synced var(--text-faint).
The system shall pass lint and type-check on all changed files.
acceptance_criteria.verification_command: npm run lint && npm run typecheck

ac_subsection_na.ci_pipeline: No CI or pipeline change; renderer token/CSS fix verified by existing lint/type-check/CT.
ac_subsection_na.hooks_gates: No git hooks or quality gates added or changed.
ac_subsection_na.documentation: design-fidelity-contract §5 already matches the synced tokens (its source is design/styles.css); no doc edit — hand-editing §5 would desync it from its source.

constraints.content: Must follow WCAG 2.1 AA — SC 1.4.3 (normal text) and SC 1.4.11 (non-text UI), in both light and dark themes.
Search for an existing utility/token before building — sync the existing muted/faint tokens rather than inventing a new one.
Prefer design tokens over literal style values; never use inline styles — changes are token values plus var() references only.
tokens.css must mirror design/styles.css (the design source of truth); token values are synced from it, not hand-picked, and derived docs (contract §5) are not hand-edited.
Renderer tier: design tokens live in styles/tokens.css; molecule CSS under molecules/.
The active-tab badge and Tabs WAI-ARIA engine must remain intact; the fix is color/token-only.

affected_areas.impact: Sync 3 drifted values to design/styles.css: light --text-muted->#6c6c75, light --text-faint->#6e6e77, dark --text-faint->#787881
Two accent-on-light swaps: active-tab label (149) and active-tab badge text (233) var(--accent)->var(--text); .tabbar inherits 149. Lines 97/326/388 unchanged (fixed by token sync)

Token darkening shifts every --text-muted/--text-faint consumer visually (Modal, Toast, Dropdown, RequestBar, TabBar, Titlebar, Statusbar, PrimitivesDemo) — affected CT screenshot baselines re-based across light+dark; Tabs CT gains contrast assertions

out_of_scope.content: Disabled-tab label color (Tabs.css:174/183, var(--text-faint)) — WCAG exempts disabled UI from the contrast minimum; left as-is (rides the synced faint anyway).
Any token drift beyond the three contrast-relevant values (e.g. the app-only dark --m-head token absent from design/styles.css) — not reconciled here.
Hand-editing design-fidelity-contract §5 — the contract derives from design/styles.css and is already correct post-sync; editing it would desync it from its source.

risks.risk: Token sync darkens muted/faint text across ~9 other components (Modal, Toast, Dropdown, RequestBar, TabBar, Titlebar, Statusbar, PrimitivesDemo); their CT screenshot baselines shift, not just Tabs.
risks.mitigation: Enumerate all --text-muted/--text-faint consumers; re-baseline every affected CT across light+dark. These are design-source-authoritative changes (intended), not regressions.

risks.risk: CT single-variant baseline misses the dark theme; a color-only shortcut could leave other drift.
risks.mitigation: Cover BOTH themes in CT; verify at runtime via design-auditor, not just static/CT.

risks.risk: .tabbar active-label inheritance assumption wrong (line 149 not inherited by the tabbar variant).
risks.mitigation: Confirmed: Tabs.css:480-481 sets only box-shadow+background; CT must assert the active-label color in both bare .tabs and .tabbar scopes.
